info.title: Agent Platform API
info.description:
Private alpha session control plane. This document is generated from the route declarations in apps/control-host/src/api/openapi.ts and the Zod schemas in packages/contracts; do not edit it by hand.

## Authentication

Send an API key as an HTTP bearer token, `Bearer <key>` (`bearerApiKey`), or use the browser session cookie that `POST /v1/auth/login` sets (`cookieSession`). A missing, malformed, unknown or revoked credential answers `401 UNAUTHORIZED`. `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/v1/openapi.json`, `/v1/auth/bootstrap` and `/v1/auth/login` take no credential.

A cookie-authenticated request with any method other than GET must also send `X-Requested-With: agent-platform-web` and must not be cross-site (`Sec-Fetch-Site`, `Origin`); otherwise it answers `403 FORBIDDEN`. API-key requests never need that header.

## Scopes

Each operation names the one scope it requires, in its description and in its `security` requirement:

- `sessions:read`: read sessions, turns, events, pending requests, usage, limits and receipts.
- `sessions:write`: create sessions and send messages.
- `sessions:approve`: answer pending permission and question requests.
- `sessions:control`: interrupt, pause, resume and terminate.
- `sessions:recover`: record recovery decisions.

What a credential holds:

- An API key holds exactly the scopes it was issued with (`--scopes`). A key issued before scopes existed holds none and must be reissued.
- A cookie session holds the scopes of the user's workspace role: `owner` holds all five, `member` all but `sessions:recover`.
- A credential without the required scope answers `403 FORBIDDEN` before the body or the resource is read.

## Idempotency

Every command (POST) except bootstrap, login and logout requires an `Idempotency-Key` header of 1–255 characters; a missing or invalid key answers `400 BAD_REQUEST`. The key is scoped to the caller, the operation and the target resource. Retrying with the same key and the same body returns the original status and body without running the command again; the same key with a different body answers `409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`. After a timeout or a lost response, retry with the same key rather than a new one. Bootstrap, login and logout ignore the header.

## Errors

Every error answers `application/json` with `{"error": {"code", "message", "retryable", "request_id", "details"}}` (`ApiErrorResponse`). Branch on `code`, not on `message`. `retryable: true` means the same request may succeed later unchanged (`REQUEST_TIMEOUT`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE`, `NOT_READY`). Each response below lists its codes and when each one happens.

## Response headers

- `X-Request-Id`: on every response, a fresh id for this request; an error's `request_id` is the same value. Quote it when reporting a problem.
- `Retry-After`: seconds to wait, on `429 RATE_LIMITED` and on `503 BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE`.

bearerApiKey.description: An API key sent as an HTTP bearer token, `Bearer <key>`. It holds exactly the scopes it was issued with; a key issued before scopes existed holds none.

cookieSession.name: __Host-ap_session
cookieSession.description: The browser session cookie set by `POST /v1/auth/login`. It holds the scopes of the user's workspace role (`owner`: all; `member`: all but `sessions:recover`). Requests other than GET must also send `X-Requested-With: agent-platform-web`.

RequestId.description: A fresh id for this request, on every response; an error body's `request_id` carries the same value.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before sending the same request again.

model.description: One of the models the profile offers (its `model` or one of its `models` in the catalog). Omitted, the profile's default `model`. Fixed for the session's life.

status.description: Filters on the status each item reports, needs_input included as derived when read.

needs_input is derived when read: a running session or turn with at least one pending request a client can still answer (open, unexpired, raised by the attempt that holds the turn). It returns to running as soon as none is left, whether by an answer, the worker settling the request, expiry or the attempt losing the session, with no change to updated_at. The event stream reports both edges as status events: needs_input right after the question that opened the wait, and the status read here once the wait ends — at the answer or settlement that ended it, or within one reconciler pass when nothing was written (expiry, a lost attempt).

result.description: For create_session and append_message: the acceptance response exactly as first returned, never rewritten; its receipt_status and status are acceptance-time values. The current outcome is this receipt's status and error; the turn's result is read from GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/turns/{turn_id} using target_ref. For interrupt: `{turn_id, terminal, no_op}` once settled, where `no_op: true` means the turn reached `terminal` on its own and the interrupt did nothing.

InternalError.description: - `INTERNAL_ERROR`: An unexpected server failure. Report it with the `X-Request-Id`.

get.description:
Answers 200 while the process serves HTTP; it checks nothing else, not even the database. Use it as a liveness probe, and `/readyz` to decide whether to send traffic.

**Auth:** public; no credential.

Runs the readiness checks in order and stops at the first failure: `database` (the database answers), `schema` (the applied migrations include every migration of this build) and `config` (required settings and limits are valid). Use it as a readiness probe: a 503 means do not route traffic here. The execution backend is not checked. From the moment the process starts shutting down it answers 503 too.

**Auth:** public; no credential.

503.description: - `NOT_READY`: A readiness check failed; `error.details.check` names it (`database`, `schema` or `config`), or is `shutdown` while the process is shutting down.

get.description:
This document as JSON, the same content as `docs/openapi.json` in the repository.

**Auth:** public; no credential.

get.summary: Check a credential and return its owner
get.description:
Checks a credential: answers 200 with the owner it authenticates as, or 401. It changes nothing; use it to test an API key before other calls.

**Scope:** `sessions:read` (API key or cookie session).

401.description: - `UNAUTHORIZED`: No credential, a malformed bearer token, an unknown or revoked API key, or a missing or expired session cookie.

403.description: - `FORBIDDEN`: Scope: the credential does not hold `sessions:read`, checked before the body or the resource is read.

503.description: - `BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE`: Storage is unavailable or the request exceeded its 30-second deadline. Retry the same request, with the same `Idempotency-Key`, after `Retry-After`.

post.summary: Create the first owner and default workspace (once)
post.description:
Creates the installation's first user, a workspace and the user's `owner` membership, authorized by the one-time `bootstrap_token` printed at install. It runs once: as soon as any user exists it answers `409 BOOTSTRAP_DONE`. It sets no cookie; sign in with `POST /v1/auth/login` afterwards.

**Auth:** public; no credential. **Idempotency-Key:** ignored.

201.description: The owner, the workspace and the membership are created.

400.description: - `BAD_REQUEST`: The request is malformed: the body is not JSON or does not match the request schema. Fix the request before retrying.

401.description: - `UNAUTHORIZED`: The submitted credentials were rejected. `bootstrap_token` is missing or does not match the installation's token; checked before the rest of the body.

408.description: - `REQUEST_TIMEOUT`: The request body did not arrive in full within 15 seconds. The connection is closed; resend the request (with the same `Idempotency-Key`).

409.description: - `BOOTSTRAP_DONE`: An owner already exists; bootstrap runs once. Checked before the token, and also the answer to the loser of two concurrent bootstraps.

413.description: - `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`: The body is larger than 64 KiB, or `message` is longer than 32 KiB of UTF-8.

503.description: - `BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE`: Storage is unavailable or the request exceeded its 30-second deadline. Retry the same request, with the same `Idempotency-Key`, after `Retry-After`.

post.summary: Email/password login; sets the session cookie
post.description:
Checks an email and password and starts a browser session: the response sets the `__Host-ap_session` cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax) for 14 days, and the expiry slides forward while the session is used. A user keeps at most 10 live sessions; a new login drops the oldest. This is for the web app; scripts and servers use an API key.

**Auth:** public; no credential. **Idempotency-Key:** ignored.

200.description: Signed in; the response sets the session cookie. `scopes` are the ones the workspace role holds.

400.description: - `BAD_REQUEST`: The request is malformed: the body is not JSON or does not match the request schema. Fix the request before retrying.

401.description: - `UNAUTHORIZED`: The submitted credentials were rejected. Unknown email, wrong password, or a user with no live workspace membership.

403.description: - `FORBIDDEN`: The request lacks `X-Requested-With: agent-platform-web` or is cross-site (`Sec-Fetch-Site`, `Origin`); every caller must send the header.

408.description: - `REQUEST_TIMEOUT`: The request body did not arrive in full within 15 seconds. The connection is closed; resend the request (with the same `Idempotency-Key`).

413.description: - `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`: The body is larger than 64 KiB, or `message` is longer than 32 KiB of UTF-8.

429.description: - `RATE_LIMITED`: Too many requests; wait for `Retry-After` and retry. Five failed logins for this email within 15 minutes lock it until the window ends (`Retry-After` is the time left), or too many logins are being checked at once (`Retry-After: 1`).

503.description: - `BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE`: Storage is unavailable or the request exceeded its 30-second deadline. Retry the same request, with the same `Idempotency-Key`, after `Retry-After`.

post.description:
Revokes the cookie session that sent the request and clears the cookie. The user's other sessions stay signed in.

**Auth:** cookie session only; no scope. **Idempotency-Key:** ignored.

get.summary: The authenticated principal, user and workspace
get.description:
Says who the credential authenticates as and what it may do: the principal with its scopes, and for a cookie session the user and the workspace. An API key has no user, so `user` is null, and `workspace` is null as well. The web app boots from this. It changes nothing.

**Scope:** `sessions:read` (API key or cookie session).

post.summary: Durably accept a session and its first input
post.description:
Creates a session for a catalog profile and repository and queues `message` as turn `1`. The 201 means the input is stored, not that it ran: follow the turn with `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/turns/{turn_id}` or the event stream. `model` picks one of the models the profile offers (its `model` or `models` in the catalog) and is fixed for the session's life; omitted, the profile's default runs. A session waits in `queued` while no execution slot is free; it is never refused for that. The receipt settles with turn `1`: `succeeded` when it completes, `failed` when it fails or is interrupted or cancelled, `unknown` when its outcome is unknown.

**Scope:** `sessions:write` (API key or cookie session). **Idempotency-Key:** required.

parameters.description: Required, 1–255 characters; a UUID per user intent works. A retry with the same key and the same body returns the original response and runs the command once; the same key with a different body answers `409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`. A missing or invalid key answers `400 BAD_REQUEST`, after the body is read.

Lists the sessions of the credential's owner, newest `created_at` first, closed ones included, `limit` per page (default 50, at most 100). Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last one. `status` keeps only sessions reporting that status, `needs_input` included. It changes nothing.

get.summary: Session detail with projection, execution and durability
get.description:
Reads one session: its `admission_state` (whether it takes input and controls: `active`, `pausing`, `paused`, `resuming`, `stopping`, `stopped`, `recovery_required`, `closed`), its `status`, the current `revision`, the execution as last observed, the number of pending requests, `attention` (why the session is held or slowed, if it is) and checkpoint `durability`. Read `revision` here and send it as `expected_revision` to pause, resume, terminate or decide recovery. `status: needs_input` and `attention` are computed on each read; reading changes nothing.

**Scope:** `sessions:read` (API key or cookie session).

200.description: The session as it stands now.

404.description: - `NOT_FOUND`: The resource does not exist, its id is malformed, or it belongs to another owner. All three answer the same, so a response never reveals whether someone else's resource exists.

503.description: - `BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE`: Storage is unavailable or the request exceeded its 30-second deadline. Retry the same request, with the same `Idempotency-Key`, after `Retry-After`.

get.summary: Estimated cost of a session and whether every turn reported it
get.description:
Reads the session's estimated provider cost and token count over its lifetime, its cost and token limits, and its queued input against the per-session limit. The cost is the platform's estimate from the model calls it saw, not a bill. `cost.complete: false` means a turn is still open or ended without reporting, so the true total is unknown; do not read it as zero. `budget_exceeded: true` means either limit is reached: no new turn is dispatched, but input is still accepted and queued. It changes nothing.

**Scope:** `sessions:read` (API key or cookie session).

post.summary: Enqueue the next input after the current turn
post.description:
Queues `message` as the session's next turn in the same engine conversation, after every turn already queued. Only an `active` session takes input; the other admission states answer the 409 codes below. The 202 means the input is stored under a new sequential `turn_id`, not that it ran: follow the turn with `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/turns/{turn_id}` or on the event stream. A session over its budget still queues input but runs no new turn (`attention.code: BUDGET_EXCEEDED`). The receipt settles with the turn: `succeeded` when it completes, `failed` when it fails or is interrupted or cancelled, `unknown` when its outcome is unknown.

**Scope:** `sessions:write` (API key or cookie session). **Idempotency-Key:** required.

get.summary: Durable event replay and live stream (SSE)
get.description:
Streams the session's events as Server-Sent Events: first the stored events after `Last-Event-ID` (all of them without it), then new ones as they are written. Each frame's `id` is its cursor, `event` its kind (`system`, `assistant`, `tool_use`, `tool_result`, `question`, `result`, `status`, `error`), and `data` a versioned envelope naming the session, turn and attempt. `question` events announce pending requests; `status` events report the session's status and, after a pause, resume, terminate or recovery decision, its `admission_state`. The stream does not end with a turn or the session: it stays open until the client disconnects or the credential is revoked. Reading changes nothing.

Reconnect after backoff with the last complete event id in `Last-Event-ID`; replay resumes strictly after that event. The stream sends a comment keepalive every 15 seconds. `410 CURSOR_EXPIRED` means the cursor fell outside retained history and the client must resynchronize from resource state; alpha does not trim events, so this response is reserved. A `result` event is engine output, not durable completion: confirm the turn with `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/turns/{turn_id}` and treat only `completed`, `failed`, `interrupted`, `cancelled`, or `outcome_unknown` as terminal.

**Scope:** `sessions:read` (API key or cookie session).

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The `id` of the last complete event received. Replay resumes strictly after it; omit it (or send it empty) to replay from the start. A malformed value answers `400 BAD_REQUEST`.

post.description:
Pauses an `active` session so it holds no worker: the running turn, if any, is drained, its checkpoint commits and the execution stops. Queued input is kept and runs after a resume. The session goes `pausing` and the receipt stays `accepted` until the execution is observed gone; then the session is `paused` and the receipt `succeeded` with result `{resulting_admission_state, checkpoint_revision, queued_turn_count}`. A session with no execution goes `paused` at once. A drain that takes over 60 seconds shows `attention.code: PAUSE_BLOCKED` with the reason; nothing is killed for it, and terminating is the caller's choice. The receipt fails if the pause cannot commit, a resume cancels it, or a terminate overtakes it. Each step is a `status` event with `admission_state` on the stream.

post.description:

The kill reverts nothing the execution already did outside (commits, pushes, API calls): the response and the receipt say `external_effects_reverted: false`. The receipt result is `{execution_gone, checkpoint_revision, unconfirmed_turn_id, external_effects_reverted}`. post.description:
Brings a `stopped` or `paused` session back to `active`, or cancels a pause that is still draining. The receipt result is `{resulting_admission_state, checkpoint_revision, queued_turn_count}`.

- **From `stopped`:** the session is `active` at once, the next worker restores the last committed checkpoint, queued input is dispatched, and the receipt is `succeeded` in the response.
- **From `paused`:** the session goes `resuming` and a new worker restores the pause's checkpoint. The receipt stays `accepted` until that worker reports ready; then the session is `active` and the receipt `succeeded`. If the restore keeps failing, the receipt fails and the session goes `recovery_required`.
- **From `pausing`, before the stop is committed:** the pause is cancelled (its receipt fails), the session is `active` again, and this receipt is `succeeded`. Once the stop is committed the answer is `409 PAUSE_COMMITTING`.

Each change is a `status` event with `admission_state` on the stream.

- `retry_restore`: restores the same checkpoint again after what made the restores fail is fixed; queued input runs.

get.summary: Current outcome of an accepted command
get.description:
Reads the current outcome of a command by the `receipt_id` its response returned: `accepted` while it is in progress, then `succeeded`, `failed` (with `error`) or `unknown` (nobody can say; `error` explains). Poll until it leaves `accepted`. `result` depends on `operation`:

- `create_session`, `append_message`: the acceptance response exactly as first returned, never rewritten. The turn's outcome is read from `GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/turns/{turn_id}` using `target_ref`.
- `interrupt`: `{turn_id, terminal, no_op}` once settled.
- `pause`, `resume`: `{resulting_admission_state, checkpoint_revision, queued_turn_count}`.
- `terminate`: `{execution_gone, checkpoint_revision, unconfirmed_turn_id, external_effects_reverted}`.
- `recovery_decision`: `{resulting_admission_state, checkpoint_revision, resumable}`.
- `answer`: null; only `status` and `error` change.

Any credential of the same owner can read a receipt. It changes nothing.

**Scope:** `sessions:read` (API key or cookie session).

200.description: The receipt as it stands now.

401.description: - `UNAUTHORIZED`: No credential, a malformed bearer token, an unknown or revoked API key, or a missing or expired session cookie.

403.description: - `FORBIDDEN`: Scope: the credential does not hold `sessions:read`, checked before the body or the resource is read.

404.description: - `NOT_FOUND`: The resource does not exist, its id is malformed, or it belongs to another owner. All three answer the same, so a response never reveals whether someone else's resource exists.

503.description: - `BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE`: Storage is unavailable or the request exceeded its 30-second deadline. Retry the same request, with the same `Idempotency-Key`, after `Retry-After`.
